purpose: Advance the Branch Flintlock-equivalent warning chain from strategic/submarine warning to the first firm visual contact on a US fast-carrier task group without yet creating a weapon-quality strike solution.
authority_note: CURRENT authority remains 1944-01-01. This file realizes only WORKING discussion events through 31 Jan noon local Marshall time.

historical_sanity_anchors.anchor: Historical TF58 trained/fueled through 25-28 Jan and approached under radar silence/poor weather; historical groups reached launch points without useful Japanese detection.

Historical Kwajalein account records a single unidentified aircraft passing roughly 50 miles astern of one carrier group before dawn 29 Jan, a useful near-miss sanity anchor rather than a Branch contact.
Historical 29 Jan launch points were about 100 miles from target; Branch operation remains shifted several days later by the existing v034/v037 mobilization ledger.

events.ground_truth: US three-TG fast-carrier force continues approach cycle with fueling/training completed or completing; Japanese Marshall network disperses aircraft, raises staged alert and narrows search arcs using submarine/DF/traffic fusion.
events.japanese_knowledge: HIGH major Central-Pacific operation; MEDIUM-HIGH Marshalls; no carrier fix.

events.ground_truth: US carrier groups and assault/support echelons remain separated enough that auxiliary/transport contacts do not reveal the fast-carrier centroid.
events.japanese_knowledge: A further outer-submarine/logistics report strengthens Kwajalein/Roi as likely primary objective but cannot identify a carrier group.
events.result: Strategic warning strengthens; no carrier GO.

events.ground_truth: One outer/middle Japanese submarine receives a strong high-speed multi-shaft sound picture in the narrowed southwest/south approach corridor and obtains a brief poor periscope glimpse of a large fast formation.
events.report: Large fast force, at least one probable flat-top and heavy escort; north-to-northeast course; speed estimate 20-24 kt; position uncertainty tens of nautical miles.
events.confidence: MEDIUM probable carrier group, not firm enough for mass air weapon release.
events.result: HQ shifts 31 Jan dawn/morning long-range search toward the reported motion cone and reserves 1-2 confirmation sorties.

events.ground_truth: A Taroa-centered long-range search aircraft, operating on the submarine-cued corridor, visually acquires one US fast-carrier TG roughly 300-380 nmi south-to-southwest of Maloelap/Taroa. Broken cloud/squalls and US CAP limit observation time.
events.report: At least two flight decks observed or strongly identified, multiple heavy surface escorts, numerous destroyers; course generally north/northeast; speed about 20-24 kt. Exact hull identities and total TF58 composition unresolved.
events.report_delivery: Structured contact report transmitted before US CAP forces the scout away; scout is lost or fails to return centered, but the report is received.
events.confidence: HIGH one fast-carrier group exists on Marshall approach; MEDIUM-HIGH larger multi-group operation; exact strike launch point still unknown.

events.ground_truth: Japanese confirmation search launches, but immediate recontact is denied by weather, US CAP and US course adjustment/EMCON.
events.result: The firm carrier contact is real but ages rapidly; no weapon-quality night-strike or first-line-carrier strike solution is granted.

Japan: Marshall bases shift from high strategic alert to carrier-confirmed battle alert.
Aircraft remain dispersed; Taroa/Roi Raiden staged-readiness is activated but no aircraft are added.
Night maritime-strike crews and reconnaissance aircraft are put on launch-ready posture pending fresh recontact.
SenTaka/middle submarines receive a time-stamped moving intercept corridor rather than a generic patrol box.
Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu carrier force remains GO-WITHHELD: one TG contact is insufficient to establish total US mission split and safe positive-EV geometry.
US: Loss/forcing-off of Japanese scout makes compromise of tactical surprise plausible to US commanders.
US CAP/ASW readiness increases; local course/launch-point adjustment is allowed.
Operation is not aborted; if fuel/weather permit, first suppression strike planning biases toward the early edge of the existing 2-4 Feb window.
information_guard: A carrier-group visual is not a continuous track.
Do not convert two observed flight decks into the total 11-deck TF58 OOB.
Do not award a Japanese strike until a fresh enough recontact survives launch-to-target aging.

next_exact_action: Resolve the 31 Jan afternoon/night recontact attempt by submarine and air assets. If a fresh carrier-group fix is obtained, adjudicate the first Japanese land-based night/predawn maritime strike package. If not, carry warning into the US first suppression strike, centered toward 2 Feb after tactical surprise is compromised.
